issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) requires a SealSaloon method named checkOrderReady(), but the provided solution implements this behavior in a method named processOrders(). This naming mismatch between the specification and the solution can confuse students about which method to implement and what signature to provide (they will expect checkOrderReady() to exist and be invoked).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent with the problem statement: rename the solution's processOrders() method to checkOrderReady(), or add a public checkOrderReady() wrapper that calls processOrders(). Also ensure the template/solution and the problem statement use the same method name so students implement the expected signature.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a method named checkOrderReady() (responsible for serving queued orders when ingredients are available). In the solution implementation the corresponding behavior is implemented in a method named processOrders(). This naming divergence for the same conceptual operation (checking and processing ready orders) creates a mapping confusion: students reading the problem will implement/expect checkOrderReady(), while the reference solution uses processOrders().
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name across artifacts. Rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady(), or add a public checkOrderReady() wrapper that delegates to processOrders(), so the implementation matches the method name used in the problem statement and reduces student confusion.
